passage: Certain deep-sea fish species can survive at depths exceeding 20,000 feet and withstand pressures more than 600 times greater than atmospheric pressure, and some researchers have attributed the evolution of these extreme pressure adaptations to increased mineral concentrations in ocean water resulting from high levels of volcanic activity during the Paleozoic era. However, there is no evidence of significant increases in volcanic activity coinciding with relevant periods in deep-sea fish evolution, such as when the first pressure-adapted species appeared, when several fish lineages underwent further adaptation to extreme depths, or when deep-sea fish reached their maximum known depth tolerances, suggesting that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: changes in volcanic activity affected different deep-sea fish lineages differently.
choices.B: volcanic activity was higher when the most pressure-adapted fish lived than it was when the first deep-sea fish appeared.
choices.C: deep-sea fish probably would not have evolved such extreme pressure tolerance if volcanic activity had been even slightly higher.
choices.D: the evolution of extreme pressure adaptations in deep-sea fish did not depend on increased volcanic activity.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of the relationship between volcanic activity and deep-sea fish pressure adaptations. The text establishes that deep-sea fish evolved to survive extreme pressures, and it notes that some scientists have asserted that the cause of this phenomenon was increased mineral concentrations that resulted from increased volcanic activity. The text goes on to state, however, that volcanic activity levels didn't increase around the time of important periods in deep-sea fish evolution toward extreme pressure adaptations. If significant periods of deep-sea fish evolution toward pressure tolerance occurred without increased volcanic activity, that suggests that the evolution of pressure adaptations didn't depend on increased volcanic activity.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because the text indicates that volcanic activity levels didn't increase at important periods in deep-sea fish evolution, not that higher levels would have affected that evolution. The text provides no information about how higher levels of volcanic activity might have affected deep-sea fish.
